text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. I understand you're experiencing hematuria and right flank pain. Can you describe the nature of the pain—is it a constant dull ache or severe, cramping waves that radiate to the groin?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any nausea, vomiting, or fever along with the pain? Have you noticed any changes in your urinary frequency or urgency?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you had any fever or chills, and does the pain radiate to your groin? I would also like to check your vital signs and perform a physical exam for costovertebral angle tenderness.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history except noted recurrent urinary tract infections. No history of renal dialysis or known genetic diseases. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works in an office setting.

speaker: Doctor

text: Given the presence of multiple cysts in the medullary collecting ducts and your history of recurrent UTIs, the findings are highly suggestive of Medullary Sponge Kidney. I will now review the imaging to confirm the classic "brush-like" or "bouquet of flowers" appearance of the dilated ducts. REQUEST IMAGES
